about.title: Helping You Achieve Better Health Naturally
about.description:
Dr. Maegan has been practicing Chinese Medicine in Asheville for ten years. Her early path began with her love of nature, nutrition, and herbal medicine as ways to find peace and healing in her life. She received her yoga teaching certificate in 2008 in Philadelphia, which expanded her ideas of health and introduced alternative views of wellness that greatly informs how she lives and practices medicine today. 

After graduating from Green Mountain College in 2012 with a degree in Environmental Studies (education-focused), she joined Americorps for two years. She taught and developed Farm-To-School programs in Vermont, focusing on nutrition education, school gardening, organic farming, environmental science, and creating thriving local food systems. 

She then attended a five-year Masters and Doctoral program at Daoist Traditions College of Chinese Medical Arts. Studies focused on the Classical teachings of Chinese medicine with 88th generation Daoist Priest, Jeffrey Yuen. She also undertook advanced studies in orthopedics, women's health and obstetrics, and cardiology in the doctoral program. 

She is a primary care acupuncturist with the ability to treat a diverse set of conditions. Her specialties include orthopedic (“dry needling”) for acute and chronic pain, psychological conditions, and hormonal imbalances. She is skilled in treating the “mysterious” illnesses that biomedicine struggles to successfully resolve, such as Long Covid, chronic fatigue, autoimmune conditions, and fibromyalgia. Dr. Maegan also has longterm, mentored experienced in supporting those going through cancer treatment. Additionally, she has studied death medicine and is well versed in end of life care. 

As a Chinese medicine doctor, she is committed to seeing her patient as an individual and not a disease, offering compassionate and effective care to every person. It is her greatest honor in life to hold space for all of those that step into her treatment room. She is dedicated to meeting each patient with the utmost sensitivity, care, and respect. 

Dr. Maegan’s other interests include Cha Dao/tea ceremony, gardening, travel, and hiking in the beautiful Appalachian mountains with her dogs.

practiceAreas.title: Chinese Medicine Treatments
practiceAreas.subtitle: Natural therapies designed to improve your health and quality of life.

items.title: Pain Relief
items.description: Reduce acute and chronic musculoskeletal pain including; back pain, headaches, and joint pain from varying anatomical or inflammatory causes. “Dry Needling” or orthopedic acupuncture is utilized for those that need it or a gentler approach can be applied for sensitive or more vulnerable patients.

items.title: Stress & Anxiety
items.description: Balance mood, improve sleep quality, and reduce stress.

items.title: Women's Health

items.title: Chronic Conditions
items.description: Chronic fatigue, Long Covid, digestive issues, Fibromyalgia, and autoimmune conditions.

items.title: Oncology Support
items.description: For patients undergoing cancer treatment; boosting the immune system, helping to manage medication side effects, and improve quality of life.

items.title: End of Life Care
items.description: Support for patients and families during the end-of-life journey, focusing on comfort and dignity.

treatments.title: Modalities
treatments.subtitle: Treatment services offered for an integrative and thorough approach to medicine

items.title: Acupuncture
items.description: Hair-thin needles are placed along acupuncture channels and/or areas of pain. This activates the desired effects of acupuncture points (specific to the treatment goals), reduces inflammation, and increases circulation.

items.title: Herbal Medicine
items.description: Formulas or supplements are chosen or created for you by the practitioner based on your individual needs. These will come in tablet, capsule, tincture, granule, or “raw” form to make teas.

items.title: Pulse Taking
items.description: A critical piece of pattern diagnosis, your practitioner will take pulses on the radial artery (both left and right) in three positions and three depths. These pulse positions are associated with all of your organ systems. Dr. Maegan will assess your energetic health, where there is stagnation or deficiency, and what meridians and organ systems to focus on by the pulse characteristics. This will generally take place before needles are placed and are re-checked at most appointments, as it is always in flux.

items.title: Tongue Diagnosis
items.description: The tongue will be checked at the beginning of most appointments. It is a microcosm or mirror of the health of the body and mind. Areas of the tongue correspond to certain organ systems. The color of the tongue body, the coating of the tongue, and characteristics like cracking or peeling, tell the practitioner what the patient’s treatment needs are to create harmony and encourage healing.

items.title: Chinese Medicine Dietary Therapy
items.description: Each person has specific dietary needs to thrive. When desired/needed, we empower and educate the patient to choose foods that balance their elemental constitution, support organs that are out of balance, and reduce inflammation. These are long or short term changes that feel applicable, without harsh parameters or judgement.

items.title: Lifestyle Recommendations
items.description: Receive advice on how to create more harmony in your daily routines to support your specific health goals (exercises, mindfulness tools, stress reduction techniques, etc.) through a Chinese Medicine lens.

items.title: Cupping & Gua sha
items.description: These types of bodywork utilize suction (cupping) or scraping (gua sha) techniques to increase blood flow to areas of tension, break up bound tissues, invigorate the nerves, and reduce pain.

items.title: Moxibustion
items.description: Often shortened as, “Moxa,” this ancient modality is practiced with an herb, mugwort/Ai Ye, that is placed on needles, hovered over acupuncture points/body areas, or put safely over the skin. Moxa is warming, moving, tonifying, and calming. It is used for pain reduction, women’s health, and to strengthen acupuncture treatments when needed for certain individuals.

items.title: Electro Acupunture
items.description: A more modern addition to Chinese Medicine based on the ancient approach of consistent needle stimulation. Gentle electrical stimulation can be applied to needle points to create more efficient treatments. This is often used for pain syndromes or nerve stimulation (neuropathy) but can be applied for other reasons to strengthen the effects of the acupuncture.

items.title: Tui Na
items.description: Chinese Medicine bodywork that is hands-on to stimulate meridians, reduce pain, and balance the organ systems.

faq.title: Questions We Hear Most Often
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before your first visit.

questions.question: Does acupuncture hurt?
questions.answer: Most patients experience little to no discomfort. The needles are extremely thin and many people find treatments relaxing.

questions.question: What conditions can acupuncture treat?
questions.answer: Acupuncture can help with pain, stress, anxiety, headaches, digestive issues, women's health, insomnia, allergies, and many chronic conditions.

questions.question: How long is a treatment?
questions.answer: Most appointments last between 60 and 90 minutes depending on your treatment plan.

questions.question: How many treatments will I need?
questions.answer: This varies by condition. Acute issues may improve in a few visits while chronic conditions generally require ongoing care.
